definition: A cervical ganglion is a sympathetic nerve-cell cluster in the neck that is part of the autonomic nervous system. In this packet, the superior cervical ganglion is described as a site of synaptic transmission and plasticity involved in sympathetic activity.

reasons: The packet only discusses the superior cervical ganglion (SCG) in rats and does not explicitly define what a “cervical ganglion” is (e.g., as a sympathetic nerve-cell cluster in the neck) in general terms.

The packet mentions sympathetic ganglia and measures synaptic plasticity (LTP) in the superior cervical ganglion, but it does not explicitly state that the SCG/cervical ganglion is located in the neck or that it is a “sympathetic nerve-cell cluster” in the way the definition claims.

The first sentence generalizes beyond the packet: it defines “cervical ganglion” broadly as a sympathetic nerve-cell cluster in the neck and part of the autonomic nervous system, but the packet only discusses the superior cervical ganglion in a rat study and does not define the general term.

The packet supports the superior cervical ganglion as a site of altered synaptic transmission and plasticity in sympathetic activity, but not as a basis for a full generic definition of “cervical ganglion.”
